recall_prompt: Say how you would find the nature of these roots — say what you compute and what its value tells you.
insider_note: Write Δ = 25 as 5², because 'perfect square' is the phrase the examiner reads. The full answer needs both words — rational AND unequal; 'real and unequal' alone is the half answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find Δ
steps.margin_note: First mark. a = 3, b = 7, c = 2. Δ = 49 − 24 = 25. Write it as 5² on the page — the examiner is looking for the words 'perfect square'.

recall.must_convey: That Δ = b² − 4ac is computed with a = 3, b = 7, c = 2 and comes to 25, a positive perfect square.
accept: find the discriminant b squared minus four a c which is forty nine minus twenty four equals twenty five
delta is twenty five which is five squared and positive
compute b squared minus four a c and it is a perfect square twenty five
discriminant kanukovali, forty nine minus twenty four is twenty five, perfect square
delta equals twenty five, positive and a perfect square

steps.why: The nature of the roots is decided entirely by the sign and the kind of number Δ is, so Δ is the only computation the question needs.
common_mistakes: Writing 4ac as 4·3 = 12 and forgetting the c.
Not noticing 25 is a perfect square.

steps.label: Nature
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Δ > 0 gives real and unequal; Δ a perfect square (with rational coefficients) upgrades that to rational. Both words matter: 'rational, unequal'. (The roots are −1/3 and −2.)
lines: Δ > 0 and a perfect square, with

recall.must_convey: That Δ > 0 makes the roots real and unequal, and Δ being a perfect square with rational coefficients makes them rational — so the roots are rational and unequal.
accept: delta is positive and a perfect square so the roots are rational and unequal
positive discriminant means real and distinct, perfect square means rational
the roots are rational and distinct because twenty five is a perfect square
delta positive and perfect square kabatti roots rational and unequal

steps.why: Δ > 0 alone says real and distinct; only a perfect-square Δ makes the square root in the formula rational, and with rational a, b, c the roots are then rational. Stating both facts is what earns the mark.
common_mistakes: Answering only 'real and unequal' and missing 'rational'.
Answering 'irrational' because a square root appears in the formula.
Answering 'equal' by mis-reading Δ > 0 as Δ = 0.
